Faraday explains that the cup forms because the heat of the flame creates an ascending current of air that cools the candle's exterior, while the interior melts.

- As air comes to the candle, it moves upwards by the force of the current the heat produces, cooling all the sides of the wax or tallow so the edge stays much cooler than the part within; the inside melts by the flame running down the wick, but the outside does not melt (evidence [3], [5]).
- This beautifully regular ascending current playing on all sides keeps the exterior cool and forms the cup; if the current were one-sided, the cup would be lop-sided and the fluid would run over in guttering, since gravity holds the fluid horizontal (evidence [3]).
- The melted tallow also extinguishes the flame at the sides, which is why the candle does not burn all down the side of the wick (evidence [1]).
- Only fuel that can form this cup serves for a candle, except Irish bogwood, whose sponge-like material holds its own fuel (evidence [3], [4]).

Faraday makes the water visible by collecting it: the heated air and products rising from the candle are imprisoned/collected so the water can be gathered and examined (Lecture II, [5], [4]). To show carbonic acid, he collects the air that issues from the end of the chimney over the burning candle, then searches the jar with a candle, producing the same effect on the taper as the air from the chimney—proving the very same substance issued from the candle, and in this way carbonic acid is obtained in great abundance, nearly filling the jar (Lecture V, [1]). He also prepares carbonic acid from whitening (chalk) and water with strong sulphuric acid, showing it is exactly the same in nature and properties as the gas from the candle's combustion, no matter how differently it is prepared (Lecture V, [3]).

Yes, the Act reaches this conduct, under section 6 (bribery of foreign public officials).

- Section 6(1) makes it an offence for a person (P) to bribe a foreign public official (F) with the intention of influencing F in F's capacity as a foreign public official [5].
- Section 6(2) requires that P also intends to obtain or retain business or an advantage in the conduct of business — here, winning a government contract [5].
- Section 6(3) defines bribing F as offering, promising or giving a financial or other advantage to F (directly or through a third party), where F is not permitted or required by the applicable written law to be influenced by it [5].
- A French ministry official is a "foreign public official" under section 6(5)(a) or (b), as holding an administrative position of, or exercising a public function for, a country outside the United Kingdom [6].
- The applicable written law is French law, since section 6(7)(a) does not apply and (7)(c) points to the law of the country in relation to which F is a foreign public official [2][3].
- Territorially, section 12(4)(a) gives the person a "close connection" with the United Kingdom because they are a British citizen, so the offence may be committed even though the acts occurred wholly in France [1].

Data Act - definition: a natural or legal person that has the right or obligation, in accordance with this Regulation, applicable Union law or national legislation adopted in accordance with Union law, to use and make available data, including, where contractually agreed, product data or related service data which it has retrieved or generated during the provision of a related service.
Data Governance Act - definition: a legal person, including public sector bodies and international organisations, or a natural person who is not a data subject with respect to the specific data in question, which, in accordance with applicable Union or national law, has the right to grant access to or to share certain personal data or non-personal data.

Both allow a natural person to be a data holder, but the Data Governance Act restricts this to natural persons who are not data subjects with respect to the specific data, whereas the Data Act places no such restriction. The status is based on a right or obligation to use and make available data (Data Act) versus a right to grant access to or to share data (Data Governance Act), in each case under applicable Union or national law.

در متون ارائه‌شده، تعداد نصب فعال خودِ کافه‌بازار برای سال ۱۴۰۰ ذکر نشده است (آخرین عدد مربوط به سال ۱۳۹۸ با 41 میلیون است)، بنابراین افزایش از پایان ۱۳۹۷ تا ۱۴۰۰ برای کافه‌بازار قابل محاسبه نیست. تنها مقایسه ممکن، نصب فعال اپلیکیشن دیوار از کافه بازار است که از 21.8 میلیون در پایان ۱۳۹۹ به 23.6 میلیون در پایان ۱۴۰۰ رسید (حدود 1.8 میلیون بیشتر)، اما این با سال ۱۳۹۷ و با موضوع کافه‌بازار مستقیماً قابل مقایسه نیست.
